702144.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂weks- (“to enlarge”). Cognate with Proto-Germanic *wahsijaną.

702165.t: According to Beekes, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ew (“again, away from”) + *to- (“that”); compare Proto-Germanic *auþijaz (“barren, empty”).

702137.t: Most plausibly from Proto-Indo-European *h₂wes- (“pass the night”) (> *h₂ews- by Schwebeablaut) + *-leh₂: it has been suggested that Tocharian A olar (“companion”) and Tocharian B aulāre are cognate and contain the same suffix.

702149.t: From *αὖρι (*aûrĭ), the old locative of Proto-Indo-European *h₂ews-r-, from *h₂ews- (“dawn”).

702163.t: From αὐτο- (auto-, “self”) + Proto-Hellenic *mətós, from Proto-Indo-European *mn̥tós, from *men- (“to think”) (whence μένος (ménos) and others).

702105.t: Has been derived from Proto-Indo-European *terkʷ-, with cognates including Sanskrit तर्कु (tarku), Albanian dredh and Latin torqueō.

702121.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂ewg- (“to lighten up”), which is likely a semantic extension of *h₂ewg- in the usual "to increase" sense.

702146.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *h₂ews- Proto-Indo-European *-r Proto-Indo-European *h₂ewsér Proto-Indo-European *-h₂ Proto-Indo-European *h₂éwsr̥h₂ Proto-Hellenic *auhrā Ancient Greek αὔρα From Proto-Hellenic *auhrā, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂éwsr̥h₂…

702139.t: From Proto-Hellenic *aulós, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ewlós, nominalization of *h₂ewlo- (“tube, hollow, channel”).

702127.t: From αὐτο- (auto-, “self”) + *ἕντης (*héntēs), from the full-grade of Proto-Indo-European *senh₂- (“to prepare, work on, succeed”) + -της (-tēs, masculine agentive suffix), whence also ἀνύω (anúō, “I effect, accomplish”), συνέντης (sunéntēs, “helper,…

702162.t: From αὐτο- (auto-) + κράτωρ (krátōr, “ruler”) (from κρατέω (kratéō, “to rule, command”) and -τωρ (-tōr, “masculine agent suffix.”), from κράτος (krátos, “power, strength”))

702169.t: Traditionally derived from Proto-Indo-European *h₂emǵʰ-w-eh₁-n, from *h₂énǵʰus (“narrow, tight”), and compared in particular to Old Armenian օձիք (ōjikʻ, “collar”), though this is controversial.

702155.t: From αὐτάρκης (autárkēs, “self-sufficient”) + -ια (-iă, abstract noun suffix), from αὐτο- (auto-, “self-”) + ἀρκέω (arkéō, “to suffice”).

702134.t: Compared with Lithuanian vilkti (“to drag, haul”) and Proto-Slavic *velťi (“to draw”). Beekes claims that the variants point to a Pre-Greek origin, in particular a form *alʷ-ak-.

702170.t: According to Beekes, a compound of αὖος (aûos, “dry”) and an element -χμ- (-khm-) from the word for earth (see χθών (khthṓn, “ground, soil”)). A similar formation can be found in νεοχμός (neokhmós, “new”).

702176.t: From ἀφαιρέω (aphairéō, “I take away”) + -σις (-sis, nominal suffix), from ἀφ’ (aph’, apocopic form of ἀπό (apó, “from”)) + αἱρέω (hairéō, “I take”).

702168.t: From αὐτο- (auto-, “self”) + χθών (khthṓn, “earth, soil”), sprung from the land itself.
